attacks.claim: The nightly job scores all 340k recipes for every pantry user in one statement on the primary, which serves live traffic. The only measurement is 41 minutes for 12k synthetic users, and at ~630k users the linear extrapolation is ~52x, or ~36 hours, so the 02:00 UTC window and primary headroom are unproven and the job could contend with production. This is fixable before build with a batching or replica-routing design, so it is major rather than a blocker.
attacks.evidence: "Staging run: 12,000 synthetic pantry users completed in 41 minutes." / "score every recipe in the catalog (340k recipes) in a single SQL statement joining pantry_items x recipe_ingredients on the primary"

attacks.claim: The score formula is undefined. 'Weighted by expiry proximity' has no function, the handling of items without expiry dates is unstated, and always-counting staples as present lets staple-heavy recipes score near 1.0. The zero-ingredient denominator is also unaddressed.
attacks.evidence: "Score = (pantry ingredients used / recipe ingredients) weighted by expiry proximity, with pantry staples (salt, oil, water, pepper) always counted as present."

attacks.claim: Gating the feature behind 15 manually entered, expiry-dated items adds setup before any value appears, which repeats churn reason #1 (38%, setup/typing). The plan targets reason #2 but does not validate with churned users that they will complete the gate. The post-cooking quantity prompt adds another recurring chore.
attacks.evidence: "Pantry Match unlocks once a user has entered at least 15 items with expiry dates." / "Too much setup / typing to get useful suggestions — 38%" / "Users are asked to update quantities after cooking"

attacks.claim: The 30% creation and 25% unlock figures are unsourced and unreconciled. Hitting 25% of MAU unlocking within 60 days against 30% creating within 90 days implies ~83% of pantry creators must reach 15 expiry-dated items, an unvalidated conversion assumption that drives both sizing and the success bar.
attacks.evidence: "Adoption assumption for sizing: 30% of MAU create a pantry within 90 days." / "25% of MAU unlock Pantry Match within 60 days."

attacks.claim: The +3 pt retention lift compares self-selected unlockers against a 'matched control' with no matching method. Users who invest in 15 items are already more engaged, so the comparison is confounded. A 30-day window also runs past the 6-week build, so the metric may not be measurable within the plan.
attacks.evidence: "+3 pts 30-day retention for users who unlock vs. matched control."

attacks.claim: No feature flag, kill switch, or rollback path is named for the new tables, job, carousel, or prompt. The rollout goes from a 5% beta to 100% in week 6, and once users enter pantry data the exit path is unspecified.

Pantry contents, expiry dates, and cooking-history quantity updates form a per-user behavioural profile linked to user_id, but the plan states no retention period, deletion on account close, or consent handling.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: retention, deletion-on-account-close, or consent for pantry_items, pantry_matches, or 'I made this' quantity updates.

attacks.claim: No compute, primary CPU/IOPS, Sidekiq capacity, or storage budget is stated for the nightly job or for pantry_matches write volume (~31M upserted rows per night at top-50 and ~630k users), so the team cannot judge whether the primary can absorb it.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: any cost, capacity, instance sizing, or budget for PantryMatchJob or pantry_matches growth.

attacks.claim: A single long statement followed by a bulk upsert has no timeout, batching, checkpointing, idempotency, retry, or alerting. A mid-run failure can leave pantry_matches partially refreshed with no defined recovery.
attacks.evidence: "then upsert the top 50 into pantry_matches" / ABSENT: timeout, retry, resumability, or alerting for PantryMatchJob.

attacks.claim: Six weeks with three engineers plus one mobile engineer covers a data model, three platforms, a 340k-recipe nightly job, a carousel, a quantity prompt, notifications with quiet hours, analytics, and a staged rollout. Week 3 carries scoring and the job with no slack.
attacks.evidence: "Squad: Discovery (3 eng + 1 mobile) | 6 weeks" / "Week 3: scoring, PantryMatchJob."

attacks.claim: Quantity and unit are collected and the 'I made this' prompt asks users to update them, but the score never uses quantity. A user with 1 cup of flour would count as fully matching a 5-cup recipe, and the plan does not say this is intentional.
attacks.evidence: "quantity, unit, expiry date" / "Users are asked to update quantities after cooking (prompt on the recipe 'I made this' screen)."

attacks.claim: Reusing the ingredient_aliases table for normalization is unmeasured. Coverage across the 9,400-ingredient catalog, ambiguous mappings, and read-time versus write-time application are not defined or tested.
attacks.evidence: "Ingredient normalization reuses the existing ingredient_aliases table (e.g. \"scallion\" = \"green onion\")."

attacks.claim: pantry_matches is recomputed only nightly, so pantry edits made during the day stay invisible until the next 02:00 UTC run. The plan defines no invalidation or freshness rule.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: freshness or invalidation rule for pantry_matches between nightly runs. "PantryMatchJob (Sidekiq, nightly 02:00 UTC)"

attacks.claim: Quiet hours are defined in 'local' time, but how local time is determined for multi-timezone users, stale device settings, and DST is not stated. This matters for the 78% US-timezone base.
No screen-reader labels, keyboard operation for web autocomplete, or progress-bar announcements are specified for the item form, the 9,400-item autocomplete, the expiry picker, or the progress bar.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: accessibility requirements for the Pantry tab, item form, autocomplete, or progress bar.

attacks.claim: Empty, in-progress, complete, and unlocked states are unspecified, and the carousel's behaviour when fewer than 10 matches exist is undefined.
attacks.evidence: "Home feed gains a 'Cook from your pantry' carousel (top 10 matches) once unlocked."

attacks.claim: Free-text quantity, unit, and ingredient inputs are not described as validated, length-bounded, or passed as bound parameters before reaching the scoring SQL.
attacks.evidence: "Users add items with a form: ingredient (autocomplete over our 9,400-ingredient catalog), quantity, unit, expiry date."

attacks.claim: There is no test strategy for the scoring logic, the staples rule, or the job at production scale.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: test strategy for scoring or PantryMatchJob.
